provenance.evidence: cors_probe: tools/probe_auth_cors.py run against the live endpoints (server-side CORS emulation); receipts: each entry names its own evidence; changes/2026-09-24-managed-auth-profiles-and-browser-track.md §5

about: Browser evidence for managed login (spec/auth-managed.md AUTH-22: a native pass is not a browser pass). cors_probe is regenerated by tools/probe_auth_cors.py: a server-side emulation of the CORS exchange a page at the given origin would make, with harmless invalid payloads. Its verdict says what the provider's headers allow (direct = a page may read the reply; relay = the browser would refuse it; unclear = rate limit, challenge or network error). It is not a receipt. receipts holds what a person observed in a real browser page, redacted, one entry per provider, method and stage.

platform_limits: A page cannot set User-Agent (Chromium drops it; the Fetch spec no longer forbids it but browsers differ). A profile whose provider requires a specific User-Agent needs a relay to send it.
fetch() from a page never follows a cross-origin redirect in CORS mode without CORS on every hop.
Cookies are not sent (credentials: 'omit'); no flow in profiles.json needs them.

claude-code.models.why: Anthropic refuses a Claude subscription token on any request carrying an Origin header: HTTP 401 authentication_error 'CORS requests are not allowed for this Organization because of its settings', with or without anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access. The same token, same request, no Origin: HTTP 200. The preflight and CORS headers allow the page, so the header probe cannot see this. Observed for one subscription account (the message names organization settings); a relay that drops Origin is required.
